subject: Immediate: CardinalPay reserved throughput deficit and GPU pool saturation
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cardinalpay.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: operations@cardinalpay.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 23:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: API errors + latency spike (CardinalPay production)

Neha / Priyom —

We're seeing a sustained spike in P95 latency (now ~2.8s, usually ~180ms) and a growing fraction of 503/504 errors for our production inference path since ~22:30 EST. Our telemetry also shows reserved-throughput measurements falling to ~55% of our committed units on the dedicated pool and large queuing depth for our reserved routes. This is causing downstream retries and order-processing delays for merchants.

We've attached a short log export and a screenshot of our dashboard. Please escalate — this is impacting live payments routing.

Example failing request IDs: rp_20261126_11, rp_20261126_42, rp_20261126_97.

Liam
VP Ops, CardinalPay

Attachments: cardinalpay_slo_logs_20261126.zip (120KB)
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 00:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Immediate: CardinalPay reserved throughput deficit and GPU pool saturation

Liam — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We’re opening an urgent bridge now.

Quick notes:
- I’ve looped in Prio (account lead) and engineering (Vivek, Marissa) for triage.
- We’ll run short-term mitigation (fallback routing, temporary burst capacity) while we investigate root cause.
- Can you confirm the three sample request IDs above and share any recent config changes on your side (model selection, batch sizes, region)?

ETA for a first status update: 30 minutes. I will keep you posted on any immediate rollbacks or fallbacks.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the severity and will prioritize.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: infra-oncall@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 01:00:00 +0000
Subject: [Internal] CardinalPay production — immediate remediation steps

On Fri, 27 Nov 2026 00:05:00 +0000, neha_kapoor wrote:
> Liam — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We’re opening an urgent bridge now.

Team — summary from customer: sustained P95 latency (~2.8s), elevated 5xx, reserved throughput reporting ~55% of committed. Queue depth rising on the rsvd route.

Proposed short-term actions (please ack and execute ASAP):
1) Enable dedicated pool burst for CardinalPay (burst policy ID: burst-cardinal-2026-11) to give immediate headroom. Need infra-oncall to manually allocate +20% capacity to their reserved pool.
2) Switch CardinalPay's production route to the compatible hosted-variant (rg-medium-quant) as an automatic fallback for new requests for the next 45 minutes to reduce tail latency. This will slightly increase token cost but preserve availability.
3) Throttle non-critical background jobs hitting the route (CS + customer analytics).
4) Start live sampling of failing request IDs for tracebacks; Marissa to fetch GPU scheduler logs and kernel contention metrics (NVTX traces).
5) Notify customer and provide ETA for next update at +30 min.

Attached: mutual_action_plan_cardinalpay_v1.docx (MAP with proposed mitigation + credits note).

Infra-oncall — please comment below when burst is applied and note any deployment or config blockers.

Thanks,
Priyom (Account Lead)

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 02:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Immediate: CardinalPay reserved throughput deficit and GPU pool saturation

Liam — quick update from the bridge:

What we did (10–90 minutes):
- Applied manual burst allocation to CardinalPay's dedicated pool (+25% headroom). Infra-oncall reports the allocation completed at 02:05Z.
- Enabled fallback routing to the compatible hosted model variant for incoming production traffic; this reduced P95 on sampled requests from ~2.8s to ~420ms within ~10 minutes.
- Disabled lower-priority background workflows that were contributing to queue pressure.
- Collected NVTX traces and scheduler logs; initial signal points to transient kernel contention during a large batch job on the same host group — those hosts are being cordoned and drained for a safer restart.

Next steps:
- Engineering will run a controlled drain of the affected host group and rebalance CardinalPay across lower-utilization nodes (ETA 1.5 hours).
- We will follow up with a short RCA within 24 hours and a proposed permanent mitigation (pinning placement + stricter isolation for reserved routes).
- As a goodwill gesture we’ll propose an offset credit for the impacted hours; MAP attached for your review.

Apologies again for the interruption. The VP of Engineering (Vivek) and I will remain on the bridge until the rebalance completes — I will share a final update when the host drain completes.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_cardinalpay_v1.docx
